key_insight: Accordion lets one mixture-of-experts language model serve five inference budgets by repeatedly executing a fixed prefix of layers, improving performance as inference depth increases.
engineering_relevance: A shared model with selectable inference depth can reduce the need to train and maintain separate models for different compute budgets.
method: Use predefined fixed-prefix looping paths for five budgets, keeping the minimum-budget path unlooped.
Jointly pretrain by sampling one budget per micro-batch and optimizing next-token prediction without cross-budget consistency losses.
Preserve all budgets through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, merging three domain experts via parameter-group merging and budget-matched multi-teacher on-policy distillation.
evidence_signal: After 3.6T pretraining tokens, greater depth improved Accordion-6B-A0.5B’s five-category macro-average across 37 tasks by 3.01 percentage points; the middle budget captured 89% of that gain with half as many additional layer executions.
watch_item: Additional layer executions increase inference work, and the abstract does not report measured latency or hardware-specific efficiency.
paper_title: Accordion: Elastic-Depth Inference via Fixed-Prefix Layer Looping
